entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Robert Hallam (d. 1417) was an English churchman, Bishop of Salisbury, and a leading royal diplomat at the Council of Constance (1414–1418). Representing Henry V’s England in the effort to end the Western Schism, he negotiated among conciliar factions while the council asserted reform and papal deposition/election powers.

Hallam died at Constance in 1417 before the council’s conclusion, but his presence marked England’s stake in restoring a single papacy after decades of rival obediences. As bishop of a major English see he linked domestic church governance to European conciliar politics.

He is remembered as one of England’s principal voices at Constance—a hinge between Lancastrian monarchy and the late medieval reform councils.
